title: Exception facts in the editor
summary: Hover, code lens and an MCP tool show which exception types a routine raises and handles
intro: Read this when you want to see, without leaving the editor, which exceptions a routine raises and which it catches. Hovering a routine adds one Raises: line (each type once, with how it is known: bound, handler, local, name, spelled or unknown); a code lens on the routine header says raises N types, handles M types (in VS Code a click lists the sites in a quick pick, executeCommand draglint.exceptionFacts; the Delphi IDE lens reads the same titles from draglint/callerCounts); the MCP tool get_exception_facts returns the same rows as exception-facts --json. ON by default; lsp --no-exception-facts switches the hover line and the lens off.

questions.ask: Which exceptions can this routine raise, seen from the editor?
questions.command: drag-lint lsp --db <file.sqlite>  (hover the routine: the Raises: line)

questions.ask: Where exactly does this routine raise or handle, from the exception lens?
questions.command: drag-lint lsp --db <file.sqlite>  (click the raises/handles lens: workspace/executeCommand draglint.exceptionFacts [uri, line] -> the sites)
